Read the 2021 Census Indigenous Population Profile

Source: R/igc.R
cnsprof.Rd

Reads a table of the Indigenous Population Profile, 2021 Census of Population (Statistics Canada catalogue 98-510-X2021001 to 98-510-X2021016), as published, into one row per geography, gender, age group, characteristic and group: First Nations, Metis, Inuit, the other identity groups and non-Indigenous people (or, in the household tables, Indigenous and non-Indigenous households), each in its own rows.

Usage

cnsprof(x)

Arguments

x

A profile table as published (a data frame read from its CSV).

Value

A data frame of class cnsprof: geo, dguid, geolvl, residence (on or off reserve, in the tables that split it), gender, age, chaid, characteristic, level, parid, rootid, sample, group, value, quality, tnrsf, tnrlf.

Details

The profile gives each characteristic in a hierarchy shown only by indentation (“Total - Highest certificate, diploma or degree”, “High (secondary) school diploma or equivalency certificate”, ...): the level, the parent and the topic's total (rootid) are worked out from it, so a share can be taken of its parent. A topic marked "25% sample data" comes from the long-form sample (sample = "25%"); the others from the full count ("100%"). Counts are randomly rounded to multiples of 5 (of 10 below 10) by Statistics Canada, and a cell suppressed to protect confidentiality (x), too unreliable (F), not available (..) or not applicable (...) has no value here; E values are kept and marked. The global non-response rates of the geography (tnrsf, tnrlf, in percent) are kept: Statistics Canada suppresses an area whose long-form rate is 50% or more, and a high rate means a larger error than the sample alone.

References

Statistics Canada (2023). Indigenous Population Profile, 2021 Census of Population. Statistics Canada Catalogue no. 98-510-X2021001. Released June 21, 2023. Published at www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/dp-pd/ipp-ppa/index.cfm?Lang=E (the site answers scripts with 403); the Wayback Machine holds a copy of that address captured on 8 March 2026 (web.archive.org, snapshot 20260308015010).

Statistics Canada (2022). Guide to the Census of Population, 2021. Catalogue no. 98-304-X.

See also

profshr, cnsstd, cnscwb.

Examples

# made-up numbers in the layout of a population profile table, for one
# place and two groups (the published tables hold many more rows)
nm <- c(
  "Total - Age groups of the population - 100% data",
  paste("Number of total income recipients aged 15 years and over in",
        "private households in 2020 - 25% sample data"),
  "Average total income in 2020 among recipients ($)",
  paste("Total - Highest certificate, diploma or degree for the population",
        "aged 25 years and over in private households - 25% sample data"),
  "  No certificate, diploma or degree",
  "  Bachelor's degree or higher",
  "Participation rate",
  "Unemployment rate"
)
x <- data.frame(
  GEO_NAME = "Lakeside", DGUID = "X0001", GENDER = "Total - Gender",
  AGE_GROUP = c(rep("Total - Age groups", 3), rep("25 years and over", 3),
                rep("25 to 64 years", 2)),
  RESIDENCE = "Total - Residence on or off reserve",
  CHARACTERISTIC_ID = 1:8, CHARACTERISTIC_NAME = nm,
  `IND_IDENT (2)` = c(1200, 900, 38000, 700, 150, 120, 62, 14),
  SYMBOL_IND_IDENT = "",
  NON_IND = c(5000, 4000, 52000, 3500, 400, 900, 66, 6),
  SYMBOL_NON_IND = "",
  check.names = FALSE
)
p <- cnsprof(x)
p[p$chaid == 5, c("group", "characteristic", "level", "parid", "value")]
#> Indigenous Population Profile, tidied
#> 
#>               group                     characteristic  level  parid  value
#> Indigenous identity  No certificate, diploma or degree      1      4    150
#>      Non-Indigenous  No certificate, diploma or degree      1      4    400
